Identity: New Horizons · NAIF -98. Positions and velocities use geometric ICRF vectors relative to the Sun. Every visible target is evaluated at the same displayed UTC using a compatible historical source chain.

Source: Pluto–Charon post-encounter reconstruction, PLU060. reconstructed geometry. Sample interpolation error is distinct from physical orbit uncertainty. Not supplied for this interval. These are sampled numerical interpolation residuals, not physical orbit uncertainty or continuous error bounds..

Sampled position interpolation error: 0.031971140009160744 km. Velocity: 0.000038716793484802766 km/s. No extrapolation across missing source intervals.

No measured attitude; spacecraft model orientation is illustrative.

Sampled numerical interpolation residuals do not bound physical ephemeris uncertainty.

Only listed compatible targets are available at historical epochs.

The nh_recon_e2j_v1 source comments quote inertial uncertainties of 200 km / 3.3 mm/s for Earth-to-Jupiter Cruise 1 and 10,000 km / 6.7 mm/s for Jupiter-to-Pluto Cruise 2 (3-D, 1 sigma). This encounter window crosses the phase boundary; no per-epoch covariance is supplied. These source estimates are separate from interpolation residuals and do not qualify other New Horizons intervals.

Illustrative inspection pose — historical attitude unavailable Antenna pointing is never inferred from flight direction. Planetary texture longitude and ring presentation are illustrative unless separately qualified.

New Horizons spacecraft reference model. Source hierarchy and materials preserved. Uniform model scale is approximately 1.11240 metres per source unit, normalized against the documented antenna diameter. Display origin is the model bounding-box center, not a qualified spacecraft navigation point.

Source sunlight direction and model self-shadowing are used with a fixed low inspection fill. The image is not an instrument exposure or a measured photometric rendering.
